method: contact sheets of all five masters (1 frame / 15 s) plus single-frame checks at each pick (/private/tmp/owb_comp/sheets/cands.jpg). Each plate is a ~6 s window from the film's own passed cut, starting at `at` (seconds in the master). The builder lays one plate per spoken line from the VO's Scribe word times (vo_compilation_v01/stt/), 4-6 s each, ~0.4 s xfade, lanczos to 1080p30 on 019/007/005. A plate may carry `windows` instead of one `film`/`at`: the line is split at the VO gap before the window's `from` words (Scribe times). Window times in v03 are read from a 2 fps sheet made with the builder's own accurate input seek (the v01/v02 1 fps sheets ran about 1.5-2 s early around 013 @380). v05 windows read on 2 fps input-seek sheets (/private/tmp/owb_comp/sheets/v05/w007a.jpg, w007b.jpg, w021.jpg).
rules_checked: intro: no plate from the first 30 s of its own film
no plate within 10 s of the film's own out point or of the stretch next to the bridge it sits in
no master window used more than twice across the compilation (picture_qa)
no chapter cards or title cards from the films (007 @345 is a card: rejected)
Orbit only where the film already had him (005 plates are Orbit-heavy; picks avoid him where possible)
v04: picture_qa same-stretch rule: no footage window within 10 s of one already shown anywhere in the compilation (stricter than "used at most twice")
v05: picture_qa at most 5 stretches per source: 013 8 -> 5 (420, 450, 505 moved), 007 3 -> 5, 021 4 -> 5; 019 and 005 stay at 5

plates.line: Nothing you can see in the night sky is permanent.
plates.what: 007 Milky Way band across a dark starfield, slow drift (319.6-326.8 clean, no Orbit)

plates.line: Not Saturn's rings.
Not the Moon, where it hangs tonight.
plates.what: Earth with the Moon beside it

plates.line: Not even the stars.
Saturn's rings are raining into the planet right now.
plates.what: 021 bright ring arcs, Cassini-style close-up (63.5-68.4 clean, mean luma ~100)
plates.repick: v05 021@60 shot (58.5-63.4) sits at mean luma 28-30 in the master and read 27.86 after the builder's push (polish_gate near-black FAIL at 0:12, qa_compilation_v03)

plates.line: The Moon drifts away from us by about three point eight centimetres every year.
plates.what: 013 'Last Perfect Eclipse': the Sun beside a cratered Moon above the clouds (382.5-390 clean, after the chapter title clears at ~382.4; the film's own push-in cut at ~386.5; first use)
plates.repick: v02 013@60 turned into a green laser burst at ~1 s and a green Earth-Moon beam graphic at 2-3 s (diagram FAIL risk)

plates.line: Our galaxy is heading for a meeting with Andromeda.
And every star will one day go out, even the very last one.
So how long does each of them have? That's this film. Five stories, one countdown.
We start with the shortest clock ... about ten trillion years from now.

windows.what: 019's antique clock face, slow push-in (240-247.9 clean)
nebula field: a star flares and goes dark (172-179.9 clean, no Orbit)

plates.repick: v01 005@345 ran into Orbit on a molecule-diagram wall at ~347 s (diagram FAIL risk, off the line)

plates.line: Every one of those clocks is still ticking. First, the rings.
So the rings have somewhere between a hundred and three hundred million years. A blink, for Saturn.
Closer to home, something else is leaving, far more slowly. Every year, the Moon moves a little further away.
plates.what: split: 013@270 Earth-Moon, then 013@139 Moon over canyon

windows.what: Earth with the Moon beside it (270-275.8 clean; cuts to a drawn orbit-line graphic at ~276, keep out)
full Moon over a canyon; verified 13 Oct on a 2 fps input-seek sheet: canyon Moon 139-143.5, then a Moon over molten Earth from ~143.5, so start at 139.0 (window 139.0-143.3)

plates.line: The Moon lets go a few centimetres at a time.
plates.what: full Moon over a rough sea (160-164.8 clean)

plates.line: But the biggest change coming to our sky ... billions of years away.
plates.what: Andromeda small and far in a dark field

plates.line: When galaxies collide, almost every star sails through untouched.
But no star lasts forever on its own. The biggest end in an explosion, and leave behind something so dense that a teaspoon of it would weigh as much as a mountain.
That's how the biggest stars end: fast, and violently.
plates.what: 007 burning star into a supernova burst (60-65.5 clean, no Orbit)

plates.line: The smallest stars do the opposite ... long after every other star has gone out.
plates.what: starfield / nebula (005 sheet tile 10-11; verify no Orbit, else 005 @165)

plates.line: So that's the countdown. The Moon ... ten trillion years from now.
plates.overlay: code_graphic_owbcomp_timeline_close (J0207), marker 3 + tick, whole timeline reads sound-off

windows.what: 007 lone white star swelling in a dark field under the countdown timeline (544.5-553.0 clean, no Orbit; disc forms at 553.5)
ringed gas giant with a far star (275.2-283.0 clean, no Orbit)
burning world in a nebula shrinking to a dim ember (290.8-299 clean)

plates.repick: v01 005@470 ran onto Orbit with constellation linework and sat within 20 s of 005's 488.05 out point; 005@275 alone was 0.3 s short of the line, so the line splits three ways; v03: closing_01a off 013@60 (green Earth-Moon beam graphic at 2-3 s) onto 013@388.3 eclipse; v04: closing_01a 013@391 sat within 10 s of intro_06 013@383 (picture_qa: same stretch), moved to 013@450; v05: closing_01a 013@450 made 013's 7th stretch (limit 5), moved to 007@544.6

plates.line: Every clock in the sky is running. And right now, we get to see all of them at once.
plates.what: 021 Saturn's lit crescent limb, then the film's own cut at 388.7 to full Saturn with open rings, held to the fade (clean to 393.2; ring-colour graphic from 393.3, keep out)
plates.hold: 2-3 s past the last word, then fade
